diagMapSingleDetail: Bright green: the area is covered by only one sprinkler.
diagRateReviewDetail: Manufacturer table rates differ. They assume reference spacing; actual application also depends on placement, arc and nozzle. Verify the layout before treating these values as incompatible.
diagBodyDetail: Check the body and pop-up height against this model’s manufacturer specifications.
diagCoverageBasisDetail: All zones and drawn irrigation areas are checked together, including hidden equipment. Areas are approximate. Sector geometry does not establish watering uniformity or account for wind and pressure losses.
diagCoverageUnknownDetail: Some equipment has no usable footprint data. The highlighted gaps are provisional; verify the models and settings.
diagDry: Insufficient coverage of the irrigation area
diagDryDetail: These parts of the irrigation area lie outside every sprinkler footprint in the project. Adjust placement, radius or arc.
diagFlowDetail: This zone needs more water than the source can supply. Reduce its demand or split it into separate zones.
diagFlowEstimateDetail: Estimated zone demand exceeds available flow. Adjusted radii or arcs use estimated discharge; verify the supply and split the zone if needed.
diagFlowMissing: Flow data is missing for some sprinklers. Total zone demand cannot be verified.
diagGeometryMissing: The irrigation boundaries could not be evaluated. Check closed outlines, holes and invalid coordinates.
diagInfiltrationHelp: Optional: enter the measured or specified intake rate for this site, soil and slope. No rate is assumed from the soil name.
diagLimited: Some checks need more data. See the information messages below.
diagMixedTypesDetail: Fixed spray nozzles and rotating-stream nozzles or rotors should operate on separate zones. Their application rates differ.
diagNoHeadsDetail: Place sprinklers and assign them to zones to check the irrigation design.
diagOverlapDetail: This sprinkler’s radius does not reach its adjacent sprinkler. Both are highlighted; the line shows their spacing.
diagOversprayDetail: The highlighted sprinklers water beyond the designated irrigation boundaries. The area is the union of their overspray, counted once within this zone.
diagPointCoverage: Drip and bubbler areas need separate wetted-area data; circular sprinkler coverage is not used to judge them.
diagPressureDetail: The selected pressure lies outside the manufacturer’s performance data for this model and nozzle. Check the pressure at the sprinkler.
diagRadiusDetail: The drawn radius is outside the published limits for this nozzle at the selected pressure.
diagRegulator: Pressure exceeds the body regulator setting
diagRegulatorDetail: The selected working pressure exceeds this body’s regulated outlet pressure.
diagRunoffDetail: Nominal matched precipitation exceeds the site’s specified soil intake rate. Actual application depends on spacing; check run times and cycle-and-soak scheduling.
diagRunoffMissing: Runoff cannot be assessed without soil, slope and a site-specific soil intake rate.
diagRunoffRateMissing: A verified application rate for this layout is needed to assess runoff for this equipment.
diagScaleDetail: Set the reference scale before checking real distances and coverage. Hydraulic checks remain available.
diagSectorRange: Arc outside the model’s adjustment range
diagSectorRangeDetail: Choose an arc within the manufacturer’s limits for the selected model.

diagSplitZones: These sprinklers have different matched precipitation rates. Separate them into different zones.

catInfo_mp: MP1000, MP2000, MP3000, MP3500 and MP Corner are multi-stream rotating nozzles with matched precipitation. PRS40 is recommended. Keep MP800 and spray nozzles on separate zones.
catInfo_mp800: MP800 nozzles serve small lawns and planting beds. Their higher precipitation rate requires a separate zone from MP Standard. See the selected model for compatible bodies and operating data.
catInfo_strip: MP-LCS-515, MP-RCS-515 and MP-SS-530 cover narrow rectangular areas along paths and boundaries. Their matched precipitation allows them to share a zone with MP Standard.
catInfo_corner: MP Corner is a rotating nozzle for site corners, with a 45–105° arc and precipitation matched to MP Standard. It is a corner nozzle rather than a strip nozzle.
catInfo_spray: Pro Adjustable 4A and 6A are adjustable-arc spray nozzles. For larger radii, use the corresponding Pro High-Efficiency models. PRS30 is recommended; keep them on separate zones from MP Rotator.
catInfo_prostrip: CS-530, ES-515, LCS-515, RCS-515, SS-530 and SS-918 are rectangular strip spray nozzles. PRS30 is recommended. Their different precipitation rate requires a separate zone from MP Strip.
catInfo_he: Pro High-Efficiency 8A-HE–17A-HE replace the corresponding Pro Adjustable models. PRS30 is recommended. Keep them on separate zones from MP Rotator.
catInfo_fixed: Pro Fixed spray nozzles have fixed arcs and color-coded radii. Check the selected model for available arcs and performance. PRS30 is recommended.
catInfo_short: Short-Radius nozzles serve tight spaces and small planting beds. PRS30 is recommended. Refer to the selected model’s performance table for radius and flow.
catInfo_stream: Hunter Stream Spray Nozzles (S-8A, S-16A). Directed streams for shrubs and beds, not a fan spray. PRS30.
catInfo_rotor: Gear-driven rotors (PGP, PGP Ultra, I-20…). Radius, flow, pressure and nozzle colors depend on the model and selected nozzle. Consult its Hunter performance table. Design separate zones from MP Rotators and sprays.
catInfo_golf: G-70-B, G-75-B, G-80-B and G-85-B golf rotors have flanged bodies. Design separate zones from landscape I-series rotors. Check model-specific documentation for pressure and inlet specifications.
catInfo_st: Hunter ST System for stadiums and synthetic turf: ST-90, STG-900 and ST-1600. Each model has its own pressure, radius and flow range; see the selected nozzle performance table. Use separate zones from landscape rotors.
catInfo_bubbler: MSBN, MSBN-V, PCN, PCB, PCB-R, AFB and 5-CST-B bubblers irrigate trees and shrubs. Mounting and flow depend on the model. Keep them on separate zones from spray nozzles and MP Rotator.

waterNcContext: Moderate water needs according to NC State Extension; not a volume allowance.
waterMbgContext: Missouri Botanical Garden classifies water needs as medium for garden cultivation.
waterMidwest: Water: medium. Reference for gardens in the US Midwest.
recCoolRoots: Maintain even moisture; mulch the root zone to keep it cool.
recShallowRoots: Shallow roots. Mulch helps maintain root-zone conditions.
recMoistSun: Keep soil moist and well drained, especially in full sun.
recMoistEstablished: Maintain evenly moist soil. Established plants tolerate some drought.
recMoistLoam: Prefers moist, well-drained loam; tolerates drought once established.
recDryDrainage: Prefers well-drained soil on the dry side. Excess moisture encourages root rot.
descBirch: Deciduous tree with white bark and drooping branches; performs best in cool climates.
descPine: Evergreen conifer whose crown becomes more open and rounded with age.
descMaple: Deciduous tree with a broad, rounded crown and shallow roots.
descJuniper: Evergreen coniferous shrub with spreading to columnar forms.
descLilac: Deciduous shrub with fragrant spring blooms; flowering benefits from a long cold period.
descHydrangea: Deciduous shrub with large flower panicles, flowering on the current year's growth.
descHosta: Perennial with broad green leaves and large, fragrant white flowers.
descLavender: Low, aromatic subshrub with summer flowers; sensitive to waterlogging.
descEchinacea: Herbaceous perennial with pink-purple flowers; drought tolerant once established.
descIris: Herbaceous perennial with narrow leaves and blue-violet flowers; prefers evenly moist soil.
descDaylily: Rhizomatous perennial with orange flowers, quickly forming dense, spreading clumps.
